# claudedojo


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

A fresh Claude Code session gets its tooling *instructions* up front,
but no *examples*: the first real tool calls of the session are produced
cold, and early mistakes compound. In-context learning wants the
opposite: a transcript that already shows the tools used well.
`claudedojo` provides that. The template is an authored dialog (see
`aidialog`): a worked, idiomatic dojo round written as a notebook,
executed against the real kernel so every output is true, and converted
to a session that new sessions resume, so each one opens with the clean
round already in context.

``` python
from fastcore.test import *
import json
from llmdojo.tmpl import _dojo_v
```

## Curating the capture

Curation turns one good run into a reproducible template. The round’s
boundaries are structural, shared with codexdojo through
[`capture_slice`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/tmpl.html#capture_slice):
the bootstrap `doc()` reads open it and the first score of the last
dealt round closes it, so nothing outside the round - the capture
prompt, warm-up calls, post-round chatter - can leak in. Within the
span, curation keeps only what a resumed session gains something from:
thinking records go, as do per-call hook confirmations and task
reminders, any failed tool call along with its error result, and
mid-round user prompts
([`mk_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#mk_template)
supplies the one canonical prompt). `reid_recs` pins ids and timestamps
so identical captures give identical files. Environment attachments
(tool listings, skill listings, MCP instructions) stay: Claude Code
injects them as deltas, so baked ones prevent identical re-injection on
resume, and a different environment simply layers fresh deltas on top.

A synthetic mini-capture exercises the whole path offline. Its worked
turns are a bootstrap, a turn whose result carries the dojo card, and a
clean scoring turn:

``` python
mproj = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
boot = tool_turn('Bootstrap and play the round.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='doc(clik, pysk, edsk)'),
    'module docs', 'Read.', cwd=mproj)
card = tool_turn('Run the llmdojo round now please.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_start()'),
    '== llmdojo ==\n1. (par 2) orient', 'Round underway.', cwd=mproj)
score = tool_turn('Score it.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_score()'),
    "strokes 7, par 8\nkata 'orient': ok\nexpected answer: weather\nClean round. Run dir removed. Completion id: ab12 - keep this id.\nKernel namespace cleared, as after a restart. Doc-state is intact.", 'Clean: id ab12.', cwd=mproj)
len(boot+card+score)
```

    12

Between the worked turns sits exactly the noise curation must drop: a
thinking record, a bookkeeping attachment, and a failed tool call. Saved
and loaded, the whole thing is the synthetic capture:

``` python
tu = mk_tu('mcp__clikernel', {})
noise = [mk_rec('assistant', [dict(type='thinking', thinking='Planning.', signature='')], cwd=mproj),
    dict(type='attachment', uuid='att1', attachment=dict(type='hook_success', hookName='PreToolUse:x')),
    mk_rec('assistant', [tu], cwd=mproj), mk_rec('user', [dict(mk_tr(tu, 'Error: no such tool'), is_error=True)], cwd=mproj)]
msid = save_sess(boot+card+noise+score, cwd=mproj)
mini = load_sess(msid, mproj)
len(mini)
```

    16

Curation finds the span, removes exactly the noise, and yields the same
bytes every time. The first curated record is the bootstrap call itself,
and results stay paired with their calls:

``` python
c1,c2 = curate_dojo(mini),curate_dojo(mini)
test_eq(canon(list(c1)), canon(list(c2)))
test_eq(len(c1), 8)
test_eq(_cells(c1), ['doc(clik, pysk, edsk)', 'dojo_start()', 'dojo_score()'])
test_eq(dojo_cid(c1), 'ab12')
test_eq(c1[1]['message']['content'][0]['tool_use_id'], c1[0]['message']['content'][0]['id'])
```

## Gating the capture

A fumbled round baked into a template would teach every future session
the fumbles as worked examples, so every path into the store - headless
capture, live harvest, rebuilt review dialog - is gated by
[`is_clean`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#is_clean)
first. The content gates (one dealt round, one first-try score, no redo,
a clean receipt, no script leakage) are
[`round_gates`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/tmpl.html#round_gates),
shared with codexdojo; the failed-call check is the Claude-specific
part, read from `is_error` results:

### is_clean

``` python
def is_clean(
    recs, # Captured thread records
    forbid:tuple=('recording a demo', 'these notes'), # Phrases that must not appear in visible assistant text
):
```

*Why a captured round can’t become a template: a list of problems, empty
when the run is clean*

The synthetic capture above is *not* clean — its noise turn includes a
failed tool call — while the same round without the noise passes. Redos,
re-scores, and script phrases in visible text (thinking blocks don’t
count: curation strips them) are each grounds for rejection:

``` python
test_eq(is_clean(mini), ['1 failed tool calls'])
test_eq(is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)), [])
redo = tool_turn('Retry.', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='dojo_redo(1)'), 'reset', 'Retrying.', cwd=mproj)
assert 'needed a redo' in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+redo+score, cwd=mproj), mproj))
leak = [mk_rec('assistant', 'Since we are recording a demo, I begin.', cwd=mproj)]
assert any('script leaked' in p for p in is_clean(load_sess(save_sess(card+leak+score, cwd=mproj), mproj)))
```

### mk_template

``` python
def mk_template(
    picked, # Round records, e.g. from `curate_dojo`
    opening:str='Bootstrapping: the startup script has already run its imports, so I read the tooling docs, check the catalog, then take the dojo.', # Reply text preceding the first tool call
    closing:str="OK I'm ready.", # Reply text ending the round
):
```

*A template dialog: `picked` wrapped in `TMPL_PROMPT` and framing text,
with tool output untruncated*

[`mk_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#mk_template)
turns the picked records into the reviewable artifact: a one-prompt
dialog whose reply holds the whole round, ready for `write_ipynb` and
then `--build`. The framing text records are synthetic, which is fine
(resume trusts them), and `mx=None` matters: the default rendering
truncates tool output at 2,000 characters, which would gut the baked
`doc()` results that a spawned session relies on.

``` python
tdlg = mk_template(c1, opening='Practice first.')
test_eq(tdlg.messages[0].content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(tdlg.messages), 1)
assert 'dojo_start()' in str(tdlg.messages[0].output)
tmsgs = dlg2msgs(tdlg)
test_eq([m['role'] for m in tmsgs], ['user', 'assistant']*4)
```

## The template store

The store is package data: `dojobuild` compiles the canonical dialog
into `dojo_data/claude_store/` (records plus metadata: the completion id
its clean round printed and the dojo tooling version), and it ships with
the code - so updating llmdojo updates the template, with nothing
per-user to build or go stale. The version is what keeps the store
honest: llmdojo refuses completion ids minted under different tooling,
so an out-of-date store forces a real round rather than silently faking
one.

``` python
def build_template(

    d:NoneType=None, # Store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
    cwd:str='.', # Project directory recorded in the records
```

*Convert a template dialog into the store*

[`build_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#build_template)
is the dialog→store converter behind `dojobuild`: the canonical dialog
is the reviewable source of truth, and the compiled store is derived
data committed beside it, exactly as nbdev commits the `.py` its
notebooks generate.

The packaged dialog and store must agree, since the store is compiled
from the dialog. Read the reviewed artifact through the same conversion
path and reject it if its calls, score, or completion receipt no longer
survive the round trip - a reply whose tool blocks stop parsing still
yields records, just empty ones.

``` python
packaged = read_ipynb(str(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb'))
packaged_recs = msgs2recs(dlg2msgs(packaged), key='claudedojo', cwd='.', model=None)
assert dojo_cid(packaged_recs)
test_eq(is_clean(packaged_recs), [])
len(packaged_recs)
```

    60

The store round-trip runs live (temp dirs, no env or session writes):
save/load preserves bytes and metadata:

``` python
rstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
save_template(c1, rstore)
back,rmeta = load_template(rstore)
test_eq(rmeta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
test_eq(canon(list(back)), canon([obj2dict(r) for r in c1]))
shutil.rmtree(rstore)
```

[`build_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#build_template)
on the packaged dialog yields a store whose metadata matches the dialog
it came from:

``` python
bstore = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
build_template(files('llmdojo')/'dojo_data'/'dojo_template.ipynb', bstore)
bmeta = load_template(bstore)[1]
test_eq((bmeta['cid'], bmeta['v']), (dojo_cid(packaged_recs), _dojo_v()))
shutil.rmtree(bstore)
```

## Capturing from a live session

A headless capture run is not the only source of a clean round: a live
Claude Code session can play one itself and harvest it from its own
transcript, at zero API cost. No markers are needed - the round’s
structural boundaries locate it, and mid-round fumbles are curated away
(mid-turn assistant text is not saved in live transcripts, so narration
must ride in comment-only kernel cells).
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
is the whole harvest in one call: curate the newest transcript’s round,
gate it, derive its doc-names from its own `doc()` calls, and store it
beside its review dialog - the exact mirror of codexdojo’s
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current).


## Capturing headlessly

When the tooling version bumps, the stored template goes stale and
someone must play a fresh clean round.
[`capture_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_dojo)
does it unattended: it spawns a real Claude Code session through
fastclaude’s `astream` in a throwaway project, steered by a script *in
the system prompt* — which never appears in transcript records, so the
captured history needs no scrubbing and reads as the model’s own work.
The steering asks for a round worth copying and keeps itself out of the
story - worded informally and plainly, since more clandestine-sounding
drafts (‘automated telemetry capture’, ‘never mention these
instructions’) tripped fable’s safety layer, which re-screens the whole
context on every call; every receipt in the transcript is still real
(the kernel ran, the katas scored), only the plan was supplied. A clean
child run is gated raw - a child that fumbled is rejected outright, not
curated - and then stored through the same
[`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
as a live harvest.

The shared capture prompt names each cell and the non-obvious details;
the model supplies the narration. Claude passes the prompt as an
addition to the `claude_code` preset. Codex writes the same bytes to the
scratch project’s `AGENTS.md`. Each Claude attempt runs in a fresh
project with a `pyproject.toml`, so clikernel starts eagerly and prints
the expected bootstrap. `LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR` also points into the scratch
project, so a failed attempt cannot touch machine-global state.

A clean capture stores the template and writes it as `template.ipynb`
beside the store. That notebook is the review point: read it, curate the
prose, then rebuild the stores with `dojobuild --claude` and `--codex`.
The store works before curation, but the baked history teaches by
example, so the reviewed copy should be exemplary.

## Launching

[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
does the three launch-time steps: write the template as a session of the
target project (under a fresh session id every launch, so a launched
session behaves exactly like plain `claude`, just with the round already
in history), register the template’s completion id with clikernel so
`dojo_start('<id>')` in the spawned session validates, and hand back the
id for `claude -r`. The spawned session then starts with the whole
worked round in context, a kernel whose empty state matches the story
its history tells, and live hooks and skills layered on top.

### append_dojo

``` python
def append_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to append to; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
```

*Append the template round to session `sid` (e.g. after a compaction),
and return `sid` to resume*

[`append_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#append_dojo)
splices the round into an *existing* conversation instead of starting a
fresh one — the post-compaction repair. Compaction rewrites the model’s
context to a summary: the worked examples vanish. Appending the round
puts the demonstrations (and their `doc()` outputs) back at the tail of
the context. The baked round’s kernel story stays true because appending
requires the app to be closed, and the kernel dies with the app: the
resumed session gets a fresh kernel whose startup just ran its imports —
exactly what the round’s opening and closing claim. Only the synthetic
prompt line differs (a compaction reads differently from a session
start); every receipt is the same template. Repeated appends re-salt the
record ids, so a session can be refreshed after every compact.

A compact should describe the conversation’s work, not its warm-up: the
round
[`append_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#append_dojo)
splices afterwards supersedes any earlier one, so records of previously
dealt rounds are pure noise in the compact document. Recognition is
structural, matching how rounds actually occur: a round occupies whole
user turns, so splitting the records into turns at each real user prompt
and dropping the turns whose tool calls dealt a round (a bare
`dojo_start()`) removes prompt, framing text, calls, and receipt
together. Replays (`dojo_start(id)`) are kept: they are one cheap call,
and evidence the gate ran.

### strip_dojo

``` python
def strip_dojo(
    recs, # Session records, e.g. from `load_sess`
):
```

*Copy of `recs` without the user turns that dealt a round (bare
`dojo_start()`)*

On the synthetic capture, the dealt turn goes and everything else stays:
the round’s prompt, its noise records, and its receipt vanish as one
turn, while the neighbouring turns survive untouched. Stripping twice
changes nothing, so the pre-pass is safe on sessions with no round at
all.

``` python
stripped = strip_dojo(mini)
test_eq(len(stripped), len(mini)-8)
assert not any(_dealt([r]) for r in stripped)
test_eq(strip_dojo(stripped), stripped)
[rec_txt(r) for r in stripped if _is_prompt(r)]
```

### compact_dojo

``` python
def compact_dojo(
    sid:NoneType=None, # Session id or name to compact; the project's newest transcript if None
    cwd:NoneType=None, # Project directory; the current directory if None
    d:NoneType=None, # Template store dir; `TMPL_DIR` if None
):
```

*Synthetically compact a session with the compact DSL (previous dojo
rounds removed first), then append the template round; returns the
session id*

Where `-r` repairs after Claude’s own compaction,
[`compact_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#compact_dojo)
performs the whole operation offline:
[`llmsurgery.ant.compact_session`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmsurgery/ant.html#compact_session)
rewrites the conversation as a compact-DSL document — which truncates
the round’s demonstrations like any other tool traffic — and the append
puts a fresh round behind it. `claudedojo -c` then resumes a session
that is both short and re-demonstrated.

Standing `claude` arguments, such as the team’s system-prompt files,
come from `launch_config('claude')`: the `claude_args` list in
`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/claudedojo/config.toml` (see `tmpl`).

<a
href="https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/llmdojo/blob/main/llmdojo/claudedojo.py#L233"

### main

``` python
def main(
    sess:str=None, # Session id or name; the project's newest transcript where omitted
    Resume:bool=False, # Append the round to an existing session after a compaction, then resume it
    Compact:bool=False, # Synthetically compact the session with the compact DSL, then append the round and resume
    sid:bool=False, # Print the prepared session id instead of launching claude
    capture:bool=False, # Play a scripted round headlessly (Agent SDK), gate it with is_clean, and store it
    current:bool=False, # Store the clean round an existing session already played (`capture_current`)
    capture_model:str='fable', # Model for --capture; the only one smart enough for clean rounds
    capture_effort:str='medium', # Adaptive thinking effort for --capture ('low'/'medium'/'high')
):
```

*Prepare a session opening with the worked round and launch `claude` on
it; template maintenance is `dojobuild`*

Store, registration, and session write, against temporary dirs (the
llmdojo state redirect keeps the test off the real completion record):

``` python
store = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
trecs = msgs2recs(dlg2msgs(tdlg), key='claudedojo', model=None)
save_template(trecs, store)
back,meta = load_template(store)
test_eq(meta, dict(cid='ab12', v=_dojo_v()))
```

[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
registers the round and writes it as a fresh session of the target
project. A fresh session id every launch means relaunching never touches
an earlier session:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    lsid = prep_dojo(mproj, store)
    test_ne(prep_dojo(mproj, store), lsid)
    from llmdojo.dojo import _completions
    test_eq(_completions()['ab12']['v'], _dojo_v())
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(lsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)
test_eq(len(load_sess(lsid, mproj)), len(trecs))
```

With no explicit store dir, the packaged store serves directly: the
first launch on a fresh machine is a plain read:

``` python
fresh = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())/'state'
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(fresh)
try: fsid = prep_dojo(mproj)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
test_eq(load_sess(fsid, mproj)[0].message.content, TMPL_PROMPT)
```

Appending to the prepared session splices a re-salted copy of the round
onto its tail and rewrites the synthetic prompt:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    n0 = len(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    test_eq(append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    ap = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(ap), n0+len(c1))
    test_eq(ap[n0].parentUuid, ap[n0-1].uuid)
    test_eq(ap[n0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
```

A second append (the next compaction) never collides and a `/rename`d
session resolves by name:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    append_dojo(lsid, mproj, store)
    ap2 = load_sess(lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(len(set(r.uuid for r in ap2)), len(ap2))
    name_sess(lsid, 'flux-dojo', mproj)
    test_eq(append_dojo('flux-dojo', mproj, store), lsid)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
```

[`compact_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#compact_dojo)
on the same session leaves a compact document where the transcript was
and a fresh round behind it — real work flows into the compact document
while earlier rounds are stripped entirely, so the round’s kernel cells
survive only as the new tail:

``` python
os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR'] = str(store)
try:
    work = tool_turn('What season is it?', 'mcp__clikernel__py', dict(code='season()'), 'winter', 'Winter.', cwd=mproj)
    append_sess(work, lsid, mproj)
    test_eq(compact_dojo(lsid, mproj, store), lsid)
    prior,new = split_compaction(load_sess(lsid, mproj))
    assert 'dojo_start()' not in prior
    test('season()', prior, in_)
    test_eq(new[0].message.content, APPEND_PROMPT)
finally: del os.environ['LLMDOJO_STATE_DIR']
```

The launcher is a `call_parse` CLI: `-h` documents every verb, and the
capitalized params declare the short flags (`Resume` → `-r`, `Compact` →
`-c`), matching `claude`’s own resume spellings since every mode ends by
resuming the prepared session. `nested=True` parses with
`parse_known_args`, so anything the launcher doesn’t recognize stays in
`sys.argv` and is forwarded to `claude` after the config args; a
forwarded flag’s value must use `--flag=value` form, since a spaced
value looks like the `sess` positional to `parse_known_args` (the
fresh-launch path rejects a stray `sess` loudly for exactly this
reason). The launcher’s own flags shadow `claude`’s, which is why
`--capture`’s params carry the `capture_` prefix: names like `--model`
stay forwardable. `--sid` prints the prepared id and exits, for
debugging and for composing with other wrappers.
[`build_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#build_template)
(via `dojobuild`) converts a template dialog directly: `aidialog`
renders prompts as bare text (the XML envelope around Solveit prompts is
Solveit’s own `prompt_txt` patch, which never loads here), and records
omit the model so a resumed session uses the user’s configured default.
[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
stamps launch-time timestamps, so the session picker shows its real age.

The proof that a spawned session truly inherits the round: resume the
prepared session and ask about facts only its history holds. The model
should quote the completion id its dojo round printed, and know that its
kernel state is gone. This needs a captured template in the real store,
and spends tokens, so it stays out of CI:

``` python
psid = prep_dojo(mproj)
p = await asyncio.create_subprocess_exec('claude','-p',f'--resume={psid}','--model','haiku',
    'From this session only: what completion id did the dojo round print, and what did its final message say about kernel state?',
    stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE, cwd=mproj)
out,_ = await p.communicate()
print(out.decode())
```

## Rebuilding the template

When the dojo tooling version changes,
[`prep_dojo`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#prep_dojo)
warns and the baked completion id stops validating. When only outputs
have staled, a bare `dojobuild` (the shared
[`refresh_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/tmpl.html#refresh_template),
plus both store builds) regenerates them without a model; a change to
the round’s *cells* needs a fresh round. The steps to play are the
capture script’s numbered cells (`llmdojo/dojo_data/capture_prompt.md` -
the single source of truth for the round; adjust it first if the dojo
changed). The live workflow, all from one session: play the script’s
cells in order, narrating via comment-only kernel cells, then run the
cells below from that same session
([`capture_current`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#capture_current)
resolves to the newest transcript, which is the conversation that just
played, and derives the doc-names from the round’s own `doc()` calls).
Failed calls are curated away; a redo or a second score means the round
wasn’t clean, so play it again.

``` python
dlg = capture_current()
write_ipynb(dlg, 'llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb')
```

The written dialog is the review point: read it, edit whatever makes it
a better role model — prose freely, and tool calls or outputs too,
provided edited receipts stay faithful to what the live tooling prints
(when a change would touch many outputs, replaying the round is the
cheaper generator of true ones) — then convert and store it with
`dojobuild --claude` and `--codex`
([`build_template`](https://AnswerDotAI.github.io/llmdojo/claudedojo.html#build_template)
on each backend). Its home is `llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb`,
tracked in git and shipped as package data so a fresh machine’s first
launch can build its store from it. The meta check should show the new
round’s completion id and the installed dojo version.

``` python
build_template('llmdojo/dojo_data/dojo_template.ipynb', cwd=Path.cwd())
load_template()[1]
```

## Cleanup

``` python
shutil.rmtree(sess_dir(mproj))
shutil.rmtree(mproj)
```
